en.heading: Third Thursday of October: the Philippine Conflict Resolution Day
en.origin: Conflict Resolution Day encourages mediation, conciliation and other non-violent ways of handling disagreements in families, communities, institutions and workplaces rather than assuming every dispute must go to court. Proclamation No. 1152, signed 9 October 2006, designates the third Thursday of October every year as the Philippine national day. Its occurrence moves on the calendar and cannot be frozen to one particular October date. The proclamation expressly refers to the 2004 Alternative Dispute Resolution Act, Republic Act No. 9285, and to community programmes promoting fair resolutions. The 2006 day is an education initiative, not a national day off.

en.purpose: Promote peaceful solutions and retain the movable third-Thursday recurrence of the official day.

La Proclamazione n. 1152 del 9 ottobre 2006 ha scelto il terzo giovedì di ottobre di ogni anno, una data mobile che non può essere fissata a un numero di giorno costante. Il testo richiama la legge n. 9285 del 2004 sulle forme alternative di risoluzione delle controversie e le iniziative comunitarie. La giornata del 2006 è educativa, non un giorno festivo generale.

en.heading: Second Sunday in January: the people honoured by Unknown Citizens' Day
en.origin: Unknown Citizens' Day recognizes ordinary Filipinos who contribute to the country through daily work, civic responsibility, kindness and service without receiving public fame or prestigious titles. Commonwealth Act No. 152, enacted without executive approval on 9 November 1936, declared the second Sunday of January every year Unknown Citizens' Day to honour the rank and file of patriotic Filipino citizens. The law's text praises people who quietly support national progress by fulfilling their obligations. Its legally defined second Sunday is movable and should not be presented as the birthday or death anniversary of a famous individual.

en.heading: June: W.A.T.C.H. Month encourages punctuality and honesty
en.origin: W.A.T.C.H. means We Advocate Time Consciousness and Honesty. Its Philippine programme encourages students and communities to treat punctuality, reliable public service and honesty as practical social responsibilities. Proclamation No. 1782, signed 21 May 2009, declared June W.A.T.C.H. Month and identified JCI Senate Philippines alongside education agencies and universities as partners in the campaign. The text asks schools and local government units to run activities every second week of June. It refers to a June month and a specific activity week, but does not explicitly say 'every year' for the month; continuing annual legal status should therefore be reviewed separately.

en.heading: 17–23 September: Clean and Green Week joins a full Cleanup Month
en.origin: World Clean and Green Week in the Philippines encourages communities to reduce waste, recycle materials and restore waterways, helping people connect environmental protection with practical local action. Proclamation No. 244, signed 3 September 1993, designated September of each year National Clean-Up Month and simultaneously fixed 17–23 September every year as World Clean and Green Week. The decree connected the programme to the international Clean Up the World movement and Philippine activities begun in 1990; the specific week and month share the 1993 act but are not the same period or independent global origins.
